title: Battle of the bands against Lunceford in Hartford
summary: The tired Basie band arrived from Pittsburgh and outplayed Lunceford, with Pres in top form.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: So one time when they was having a battle of the bands, we were supposed to battle Jimmy Lunceford. Jimmy Lunceford drove from -- he had come out of the Cotton Club in his bus, oh, he had the big Greyhound air-conditioned bus, in Hartford,
Connecticut. And we came from Pittsburgh. Doggone, a long ride from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania to Hartford, Connecticut. And we were so tired. Gee whiz.

Basie said, "Well, I'm tired like everybody else, you know." And most of the guys in Jimmy Lunceford's band didn't even speak. Willy Smith was one of the most warmest guys and Joe Thomas, and some of them, you know -- here Count Basie, we got out of the bus, was ragged, you know. But we got on the bandstand, we started popping. We started shying down. Dolgarn, before you know it, Jimmy Lunceford was coming up to the bandstand. All the guys was coming up, you know. So we put a hurting on him that night. Oh, we washed him out of it, the whole dancehall. Pres played like he'd never played before. Oh, he played, doggone it.
Well, that's like, you know, Harry Carney says the only band that washed Duke's band out was Fletcher Henderson's and he said that was when they let Coleman Hawkins play practically all night.
He said that took care of that.
That took care of that, veah. He had a homerun everytime Coleman played, you know. That's with -- well, Basie had a good band, though. We had some arrangements that was, oh, it was mean.
Do you think sometimes you played
Lot of times. Lot of times. You get that-
Yeah, somebody was saying, I think it was Jay McShann said to me. "The trouble is they get off the bus, eat a big dinner, have a full stomach, sluggish."
Yeah, lazy. Lazy. But you get off the bandstand tired, gee whiz, have a chance to grab a sandwich, you know, not a meal, get right on the bandstand.
But Basie had a band, though. Even the head arrangements that we had, they sounded good because we had them together, you know.
